caption:
A DCT (Volkswagen and Skoda call theirs DSG) is basically two automated clutches. It's quick and efficient, but it doesn't like being half-engaged for long, which is exactly what bad stop-go habits do.

Fix three habits and a DCT is perfectly happy in Indian traffic. And if you ever see a gearbox heat warning on the dash, pull over safely and let it cool.

DCT owners, which habit were you guilty of? 👇

slides.heading: You're driving your DCT wrong in traffic
Don't hold slopes with throttle
slides.body: Balancing on an incline with the accelerator slips the clutches and heats them. Use the brake or auto hold.

slides.heading: Don't creep inch by inch
slides.body: Constant crawling keeps clutches half-engaged. Wait for a gap, then move in one go.

slides.heading: Brake firmly at signals
slides.body: Foot firmly on the brake when stopped, or use auto hold if your car has it.

slides.heading: So, is a DCT safe in traffic?
slides.body: Yes, with these habits. Heat warning on the dash? Pull over safely and let it cool.

voice_lines: Driving your DCT wrong in traffic? The biggest mistake is holding the car on a slope with the accelerator.
Crawling forward inch by inch keeps the clutches half engaged. I'd rather wait for a gap and move once.
At signals, keep your foot firmly on the brake, or use auto hold if your car has it.
So yes, a DCT is fine in traffic with these habits. Follow for more automatic gearbox tips.
